name: Dataset Pipeline
tagline: A customizable pipeline for training-ready datasets.
description: A customizable Python pipeline for downloading, cleaning, filtering, validating, deduplicating, analyzing, and exporting datasets for machine-learning and model fine-tuning workflows.

organization.name: Kode Developers
organization.description: A customizable dataset preparation and processing pipeline built by Kode Developers.

challenge: Machine-learning datasets often use different schemas, field names, languages, metadata formats, licenses, and quality standards. Preparing multiple datasets manually makes it difficult to maintain consistent training data and reliably track rejected samples, duplicates, statistics, and processing progress.
solution: Dataset Pipeline provides a configurable processing workflow that standardizes datasets into a unified structure and applies consistent cleaning, filtering, validation, deduplication, statistics, logging, and export steps.

currentConfiguration.importantNote: Six datasets are currently configured in the project. This is the current configuration, not a hard limit of the pipeline. Dataset selection is customizable.

datasets.name: EvolCode
datasets.note: Currently configured but rejected by the active license filter because its license is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, which is not included in the pipeline's currently allowed license list.

pipelineStages.name: Dataset Download
pipelineStages.description: Downloads datasets from Hugging Face using the Hugging Face datasets library, with streaming and non-streaming support, retry handling, and fallback loading for supported raw dataset formats.

pipelineStages.name: Dataset-Specific Preprocessing
pipelineStages.description: Uses dataset-specific adapters to extract relevant fields and normalize them into the pipeline's unified structure.

pipelineStages.name: Cleaning
pipelineStages.description: Handles line-ending normalization, trailing whitespace, excessive blank lines, invalid UTF-8, empty output, and null-byte content.

pipelineStages.name: Language Filtering
pipelineStages.description: Normalizes language aliases such as py, js, c++, and golang, then keeps configured supported languages. Unknown or missing languages are rejected.

pipelineStages.name: License Filtering
pipelineStages.description: Normalizes common license aliases and rejects missing, unknown, or disallowed licenses.

pipelineStages.name: Quality Filtering
pipelineStages.description: Detects and rejects autogenerated content, minified content, highly repetitive code, and suspicious control characters.

pipelineStages.name: Validation
pipelineStages.description: Validates required fields, data types, token limits, non-empty instructions, non-empty outputs, and UTF-8 validity.

pipelineStages.name: Merge
pipelineStages.description: Combines accepted samples from the configured datasets.

pipelineStages.name: Deduplication
pipelineStages.description: Performs exact and near-duplicate detection using MinHash and MinHashLSH globally across the merged dataset.

pipelineStages.name: Statistics
pipelineStages.description: Collects sample counts, token counts, average, minimum and maximum tokens, language distribution, source distribution, and rejection information.

pipelineStages.name: Export
pipelineStages.description: Exports processed training data as JSONL.

features.title: Customizable dataset workflow
features.description: Configure dataset selection, sources, processing settings, filtering rules, workers, retries, checkpoints, and export behavior.

features.title: Unified dataset normalization
features.description: Dataset-specific adapters transform varied source schemas into a consistent internal structure for downstream processing.

features.title: Quality and policy filtering
features.description: Consistent language, license, content-quality, required-field, UTF-8, and token-limit checks identify unsuitable samples.

features.title: Global deduplication
features.description: Exact and near-duplicate output or code content is compared across the merged dataset with MinHash and MinHashLSH.

features.title: Detailed observability
features.description: Logging and rejection reporting cover processing progress, accepted and rejected samples, filtering reasons, checkpoints, and export summaries.

features.title: Checkpoint-aware export
features.description: Resume support tracks processing state and exports training-ready JSONL data with a configurable validation split.

observability.title: Logging & Observability
observability.description: The pipeline includes detailed logging and rejection reporting so processing progress and filtering decisions can be inspected instead of treating dataset transformation as a black box.

configuration.retention: Keep first occurrence and reject later duplicates

recordedRun.label: Recorded Pipeline Run
recordedRun.note: These figures represent a recorded run of the current pipeline configuration. They are not permanent project totals, guaranteed output, or benchmark results.

technicalHighlights.title: Configurable processing
technicalHighlights.description: Dataset selection, source IDs, splits, filtering, tokenization, deduplication, workers, retries, logging, checkpoints, and export settings can be customized.

technicalHighlights.title: MinHash deduplication
technicalHighlights.description: MinHash with 128 permutations and a 0.90 MinHashLSH threshold compares output/code content globally across merged datasets while retaining the first occurrence.

technicalHighlights.title: Tokenizer limits
technicalHighlights.description: The Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B tokenizer counts instruction, input, and output together against configurable 20-token minimum and 32,768-token maximum limits.

technicalHighlights.title: Checkpoint and rejection tracking
technicalHighlights.description: Checkpoint files support resume behavior and record processing state, while rejection reporting preserves filtering and validation reasons.
